body:
Fixes #211

## Summary

Add public geometry/solver/SVG/raster providers backed by isolated, transactional snapshots, and let `<links-network>` display and export the same provider scene. Large decimal indexes and LiNo settings survive partial updates, including navigation while geometry is pending. Stale jobs cannot overwrite committed frames or solver pins. Element `ready` includes provider updates and solves; failed jobs emit `layouterror`, populate diagnostics and preserve the prior frame. PNG/JPEG/WebP encoding has an explicit JPEG matte and bounded allocation.

Add declarative independent pixel corners/edges, state overrides and explicit frame inheritance at all ten requested levels. Material opacity belongs to a separate clipped surface layer. Optical parameters are host hooks, and appearance presets preserve viewer preferences. An opt-in effect governor controls animation and sound sinks.

This remains a **draft**. Framework bridge tests do not prove the consumer's exact geometry, collision, caption/font/export, shader/audio or twelve-palette contracts. The default geometry backend and legacy `frameStyle` behavior remain available. No consumer implementation, test, artwork or palette was copied. The [requirement inventory](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/issue-211-26fd651393e3/docs/case-studies/issue-211/README.md) explicitly records unfinished criteria.

## Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Geometry/export/solver extension points and solved-frame parity | `presentation.test.js`: identical provider SVG for preview/export, detached snapshots, stale solver cancellation, retained pins, committed revisions, failed jobs, pending-setting navigation, element readiness, failure events and diagnostics recovery |
| Large indexes and persistent geometry/style settings | Decimal strings beyond safe Number range, official LiNo parsing, retained partial updates and nested LiNo export |
| Legacy PNG export dimensions | A 5,000 × 4,000 mock-canvas regression fails with the new API cap before the compatibility fix and passes afterward; no real pixel buffer is allocated |
| SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP interface | `raster-export.test.js`: MIME types, JPEG matte, bounds validation and URL cleanup |
| Independent frame sizes, strokes, edges, states and levels | `frame-schema.test.js`: explicit inheritance, independent overrides, sizes above 48 pixels, tiny-element fitting, invalid/cyclic schema rejection |
| Transparent optical surface composition | Original example below; Chromium and WebKit accessibility/structure/screenshot regression tests |
| Viewer comfort and idle animation/audio | `material-surface.test.js`: preference preservation, reduced motion, visibility cancellation, idle frames and sound volume |
| Exact consumer curve/marker/solver/caption/font/export parity | **Unfinished.** Mock providers verify only the public bridge contract. Consumer adapters must remain until their real contracts pass. |
| Twelve complete consumer palettes and optical engine parity | **Unfinished.** Existing themes are retained; host hooks do not establish consumer parity. |

Repository licensing policy explicitly denies copying from `konard/konard.github.io` while it has no license. The license API returns 404 and the repository metadata still reports `license: null` (rechecked November 7, 2026), and [consumer PR 55](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/pull/55) retains its compatibility adapters and licensing prerequisite. An owner licensing decision or independently implemented and verified replacements are needed for the remaining parity criteria. The extension tests are not presented as substitutes for those contracts.

The readiness regression reproduced both stale `ready` and missing `layouterror` before the fix; the same tests pass afterward. This verifies the bridge lifecycle, not consumer solver behavior.

## Reproduction and visual evidence

Build and open `examples/themes/optical-frames/index.html` as described in its README. Append `?before` for the shared-corner helper; omit it for independently configured corner/edge strokes and optical layers. These are original framework screenshots, not consumer parity screenshots.

Before:

![Shared-corner helper](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/issue-211-26fd651393e3/docs/case-studies/issue-211/before.png?raw=true)

After:

![Independent optical frames](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/blob/issue-211-26fd651393e3/docs/case-studies/issue-211/after.png?raw=true)

## Validation

- Focused regressions: passing (15 cases reported as tests across the new Node suites).
- Chromium and WebKit optical-frame browser/accessibility tests: passing; reviewed screenshot baselines included.
- `66bccac`: `npm test` passed (4,130 passed, 10 skipped); `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:duplication` passed. The full suite used two CPU cores and a 1 GiB Node heap cap to bound local resources. CI passed completely on `66bccac`: all nine workflows completed successfully, with 60 successful checks and 11 intentional skips. The full browser suite passed 535 tests, the repeated WebKit overlay matrix passed 39 tests, and native web keyboard/accessibility checks passed 2 tests. [Browser run](https://github.com/link-foundation/ui/actions/runs/42323196500).

## Checklist

- [ ] Every acceptance criterion of the issue is met and checked above.
- [x] CI is green at the pushed revision, including all required gates.
- [x] Changeset names both changed published packages.
- [x] Original visual example and before/after screenshots are included.
- [x] No unlicensed consumer material or new dependency was introduced.
- [x] Existing features and backend APIs are preserved.

Do not merge or release this draft while the unfinished parity criteria remain.
title: Add network backend providers and independent optical frames
